source: The author's own test runs with scripts/hwqual.py, logged per message; summary in docs/HARDWARE-TESTS.md

connections: DIN MIDI through a USB MIDI interface

firmware.note: Built by the author from the stock OS 1.54 file; not read back from the device.

results.what: all eight MIDI tracks, pitch bend, aftertouch, mod wheel and breath, every value against a model of the sums
results.result: pass, DIN and USB, both outputs identical

results.what: V.SNS 100/50/25/0 %, velocity routes before their note
3,000 random messages to all eight tracks

results.result: USB-USB 0.9 ms, DIN-USB 1.9 ms, USB-DIN 2.0 ms, DIN-DIN 2.9 ms

results.what: sequencer started over MIDI, live input while playing
300 live pitch bends and 300 stock notes each with the clock stopped, running, sequencer playing, a clock byte inside a message
results.result: pass over USB; over DIN pass once the interface fault below was kept out

results.what: 15,511 messages in 20 s to all eight tracks, sequencer at 160 BPM (USB)
results.result: pass: no stuck notes, well formed, model exact afterwards, UI kept up

results.what: project load, power cycle, unsaved change, CREATE NEW with default presets
page, TRIG hold, BEND, preset menu and naming, audio tracks by ear

limitations: The test MIDI interface drops a DIN message that follows a clock byte within about 0.3 ms (scripts/loopback.py: 300 of 300 with no Digitakt connected); DIN losses with clock were traced to it, not the mod.
A loose DIN cable corrupted bytes in one session; those runs were discarded.
Run on one unit; Digitakt 2 and OS 1.53 not tested.
